comparison: Perfect agreement on β-d-glucan as diagnostic marker for PCP (C29-C32). Both evaluations find the evidence convincing and well-supported by data in Figure 1A-B.
Complete agreement on basic T cell phenotyping results (C38-C42). Both accept the findings, though OpenEval notes some comparisons lack clear statistical significance and show high variability.
Both accept B cell population findings (C58-C61). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of statistical significance and low proportions, while peer reviewers accept without challenge.
Complete agreement on comparative analysis using public COVID-19 data (C72-C75). Both view this as adequate for addressing absence of healthy controls and strengthening biological plausibility.

Both acknowledge study limitations (C110-C114). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED for transparency. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, expressing fundamental concerns about lack of baseline controls and requesting more thorough analysis.

Strong agreement on myeloid cell analysis (C52-C57, with C56 shared). Both accept the detailed characterization, though OpenEval notes functional implications remain unclear and one PCP case exclusion could introduce bias.
Agreement on KL-6 biomarker findings (C33, C35-C37). Both accept results despite lack of statistical significance. OpenEval notes KL-6 appears less discriminatory than β-d-glucan.

Both strongly support CD16+ T cell expansion in PCP (C43-C47 from OpenEval; C44-C47 overlap with peer R2). OpenEval emphasizes Citrus analysis rigor and novelty. Peer reviewers find evidence convincing for correlation with PCP severity.

Overlapping coverage of CD16+ T cell correlation analysis (C69-C71). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to borderline significance (p=0.053) and small sample size. Peer reviewers accept the correlation findings as convincing.

Both address fatal PCP case with dramatic CD16+ expansion (C65-C66). OpenEval notes striking 97.5% expansion but cautions it's single case. Peer reviewers incorporate this into overall acceptance of CD16+ correlation with severity.

Agreement on ICI-ILD T cell phenotypes (C48-C50, C92). OpenEval supports findings from Citrus analysis but notes functional significance requires investigation. Peer reviewers find evidence convincing for CD57+ CD8+ T cell infiltration.

Agreement on FCRL5+ B cells in ICI-ILD (C62-C63). Both accept the finding. OpenEval notes statistical significance not explicitly stated and mechanistic role speculative. Peer reviewers find evidence convincing.

Agreement on CCR2+ CCR5+ CD14+ monocytes in ICI-ILD (C107, C56, C13). Both accept findings. OpenEval notes M1-like phenotype inference lacks direct functional characterization. Peer reviewers find evidence convincing.

Partial overlap on ICI-ILD mechanisms (C92-C96 from OpenEval; C92 in peer R3). OpenEval supports data but notes mechanistic conclusions speculative. Peer reviewers accept overall ICI-ILD findings as convincing.
